conditions: Real-valued random variable X has finite support consisting of distinct real values x_i, i=1,...,n, with n a positive integer; probabilities sum to one; mu=E[X].

evidence: Variance is the expectation of (X-mu)^2 with mu=E[X]. Apply the finite discrete expectation formula to this function of X: each possible value contributes its squared deviation times its probability. This is not the unweighted sample variance.

Reference cross-check: https://openstax.org/books/introductory-statistics-2e/pages/4-2-mean-or-expected-value-and-standard-deviation. Checked 2026-11-27. Proposed maintainer approval; not independent human certification.
